Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · Work & responsibility

pressure noun

being pressed, urged

also under pressure, put pressure on, pressurize, be pressed, keep at someone, press on, keep at it, urge (verb)

classical

Cic. Att. 4.5.1: urgēbar ab eō ad quem mīsī
Cic. Fam. 9.1.1: tot tantīsque rēbus urgēmur
Traupman 401

urgeō, urgēre, ursī

verb, second conjugation

press hard, urge; (passive) be under pressure

Latin uses the verb: to be under pressure is urgērī; to put pressure on someone, urgēre or īnstāre.

Other words

  • īnstō, īnstāre, īnstitī — press, insist, keep at (someone)

    verb, first conjugation: with the dative; ut and the subjunctive · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 1.13.3: īnstat et urget Catō; Cic. Att. 13.32.1: urgē, īnstā, perfice (Lewis & Short); Traupman 364

Examples

  • urgēbar ab eō ad quem mīsī, et nōn habēbam exemplar

    I was under pressure from the man I sent it to, and I had no copyCic. Att. 4.5.1

  • īnstat et urget Catō

    Cato keeps up the pressureCic. Att. 1.13.3

  • etsī tot tantīsque rēbus urgēmur, ut nūllam adlevātiōnem quisquam nōn stultissimus spērāre dēbeat

    although we are under such pressure from so many great troubles that only a fool would hope for any reliefCic. Fam. 9.1.1

  • Urgē, īnstā, perfice.

    Keep at it, press on, finish the job.Cic. Att. 13.32.1 (Lewis & Short s.v. īnstō)

  • Īnstā, perfice!

    Press on and finish the job!Traupman 364

See also force, pressure.
